MCP Console provides a live R, Python, and SQL session for data analysis: a place to load data once, explore questions, refine plots, read help, and debug code with the relevant objects still in memory.
Console brings the interactive tools of a REPL to agents through one compact MCP tool, `send`.

Code runs in an [OS-level sandbox](SANDBOX.md) by default, with controls over filesystem writes and direct network access for long-running and unattended work.
Automatic environment and package preparation lets you start without a Console configuration file.

## Work interactively, keep useful state

Data analysis rarely follows a straight line.
An agent can keep data, models, and intermediate results in memory, then follow the next useful question instead of rerunning a script from the beginning.
It can inspect a rendered plot before refining it, or pause in a debugger and evaluate code against live objects.

Long-running computations can continue between tool calls; the agent can collect results later or interrupt the work while keeping the session.
Output previews limit how much text enters the model's context, while [recordings](RECORDING.md) keep logs and plots available for later inspection.

## R, Python, and SQL, together or separately {#one-workspace-three-languages}

Use the languages a task calls for, individually or in combination.
The built-in runtimes are embedded in a single worker process, and data can move between languages without intermediate files.
Explore in one language, query with SQL, and plot in another without rebuilding the dataset at each step.
See [Working with R, Python, and SQL](BUILTIN_RUNTIME.md).

## Start without a configuration file

Install Console, connect your MCP client, and start working.
By default, Console prepares a managed Python environment and common data packages, and can resolve additional packages as code needs them.
You can also [select an existing project environment](CONFIGURATION.md).
See [Get started](getting-started.qmd) for installation prerequisites and client setup, or [Requirements and environments](REQUIREMENTS.md) for package preparation.

Console uses MCP rather than a provider-specific API.
Use it with Codex, Claude Code, or another MCP-compatible client without tying the workspace to a model provider.

## Where Console fits

- **Unattended agents:** carry long-running analysis through to results within configured sandbox permissions.
- **Model evaluations:** give agents a persistent data-analysis environment for realistic evaluation tasks.
- **Conversational analysis:** let the agent work in its own session while you focus on questions and results, rather than a shared code editor.
- **Large-data investigations:** load a dataset once and keep intermediate results as new questions arise.
- **Debugging and package development:** pause execution, inspect live objects, and evaluate code where a failure occurs.

## Status and trust

Console is a **development preview** for macOS, Linux, and [experimental Windows x64](WINDOWS.md).
Run it alongside the MCP client on the intended execution host.

The default sandbox permits regular-file writes only in private temporary storage and restricts direct networking, but permits host-file reads.
**Readable secrets are not protected.** Project configuration is trusted input and may widen permissions.
Dependency preparation has a separate policy.
Recordings contain input and output without redaction and have no automatic cleanup.
See [Sandbox and trust](SANDBOX.md) before changing permissions and [Recordings and reports](RECORDING.md) before sharing session files.
